items.title: Growth is cracking while long yields stay high
items.detail: September payrolls +29k (vs ~85-90k), unemployment 4.2%, wages +0.1% m/m, July-August revised down 60k — yet the 10-year closed ~5.28% after touching a 24-year high this week and the 30-year ~5.63%. Weak growth with sticky yields is the stagflation mix that de-rates long-duration equities.

items.title: Leadership is very narrow
items.detail: Only 2 of 11 S&P sectors (tech, energy) closed above their 50-day averages on Oct 2; real estate (-7.1%), utilities (-6.7%) and financials (-5.8%) sit deep below theirs. The Dow had its worst week since March (-1.3%) while the Nasdaq rose. A single AI disappointment would hit an index that is leaning on one theme.

items.title: Oil and war remain a binary
items.detail: The Middle East war is in its eighth month; the US is reportedly sending another carrier and 10,000 personnel to the Gulf. The G7 agreed on Oct 2 to release 100m barrels of crude and diesel (US diesel ~$6.37). WTI fell 1.9% to $91.11 Friday; Brent ~$102. Escalation re-ignites inflation; a deal hits the book's energy names.

items.title: Fed path re-pricing both ways
items.detail: October hike odds fell from ~64% to ~16-23% after the jobs report, and two Fed officials said they need time. This week's Fed minutes (Wed) and CPI (Thu) can swing that back fast — August CPI was 3.4%.

items.title: Bank earnings into a de-rated sector
items.detail: Financials fell ~2.5% on the week and the bank ETF lost ~6.1% in September as yields backed up; Q3 trading will not repeat Q2's boom. JPM and WFC open the season this week (per calendar previews).

items.title: Insiders selling into AI and cyber highs
items.detail: CrowdStrike's President sold ~$64.2m on Sep 30 near the record; CoreWeave's CEO and two executives sold ~$17.6m at $87.69. Micron's margin-guide miss shifted the memory debate to 'how long can it stay this good'.

items.title: Consumer discretionary softening
items.detail: Nike's Oct 1 call warned weak sportswear demand will persist and could force discounting; LULU and UA sit near 52-week lows. DKS insiders are the counter-signal at ~$130.
